web.title: Shaadi Hai Housie: Kitty Party Tambola Twist, Rules and Variations
web.description: Shaadi Hai Housie is a tambola twist for kitty parties: on secret shaadi date numbers everyone passes her ticket left. Rules, scoring, variations and FAQ.
web.intro: Shaadi Hai Housie is a Housie (tambola) twist for a kitty party where the host secretly picks five "shaadi date" numbers, and every time one of them is called she shouts "Shaadi hai!" and every lady passes her ticket, cuts and all, to the lady on her left. You win by claiming Jaldi Five, a line or Full House on whichever ticket is in your hands at that moment, so a nearly full ticket can walk away from you just before the end. It is played with normal Housie tickets, pens and a bowl of number chits, and it fits the December shaadi season perfectly.
materials: One Housie (tambola) ticket per lady, printed or old ones
A katori or bowl with number chits from 1 to 90 (or a number calling app on the host's phone)
One small chit for the host's 5 secret shaadi dates
A small table in the middle for the bowl
Small prizes for Jaldi Five, lines and Full House
steps: Seat all the ladies in a circle and give each one a Housie ticket and a pen.
Before starting, the host secretly writes 5 numbers between 1 and 15 on a small chit. These are the shaadi dates. She shows the chit to nobody.
The host plays normal Housie: she draws a number chit from the bowl, calls it out, and everyone cuts it if it is on her ticket.
Whenever the called number is one of the shaadi dates, the host shouts "Shaadi hai!" right after calling it.
On "Shaadi hai!", every lady first cuts the number if she has it, then passes her ticket to the lady on her left. Cuts stay on the ticket.
Everyone keeps playing on the ticket she now holds. A ticket can change hands up to 5 times in one game.
Claims for Jaldi Five, top, middle and bottom lines and Full House are made on the ticket in your hands. The first correct Full House wins the game.
rules: Pass your ticket at once when the host says "Shaadi hai!"; holding it back costs a Rs 10 fine into the kitty pot.
Do not cut a new number while tickets are being passed; such a cut is cancelled.
Every claim is checked by the host against the called numbers.
A wrong claim puts that ticket in the middle and its holder sits out one round.
The prize goes to whoever is holding the winning ticket, not to the lady it started with.
variations: Kharmas date: make the last shaadi date "Kharmas". When it comes up, the game freezes for 10 seconds and the lady with the most-cut ticket must do one baraat dance step before anyone can claim.
Vidaai: on a second secret list of numbers the host shouts "Vidaai!" and tickets go to the right instead.
Double shaadi: on one special number tickets move two places to the left.
Pick the shaadi dates from real December wedding dates the group has, so the room cheers when "their" date comes up.
tips: Keep all 5 shaadi dates between 1 and 15 or in the first numbers you call, so the swapping starts early and keeps going.
Ask ladies to write nothing on the tickets except cuts, so tickets can move freely.
Use a pen that writes clearly so the next lady can see the cuts.
Sitting in a proper circle makes "pass to the left" easy and quick.
Announce the twist before the game but never the dates; the surprise is the fun.

faq.q: How many players do you need for Shaadi Hai Housie?
faq.a: It works for 8 to 20 ladies sitting in one circle. With more players, make two circles with one host each.

faq.q: What do you need to play Shaadi Hai Housie?
faq.a: Housie tickets, a pen for every lady, a bowl of number chits from 1 to 90 (or a calling app) and one small chit for the host's 5 secret shaadi dates.

faq.q: How is Shaadi Hai Housie different from normal tambola?
faq.a: Calling and claiming are the same, but when a secret shaadi date number is called, everyone passes her ticket to the left with its cuts. You claim on the ticket you hold at that moment.

faq.q: How long does a game of Shaadi Hai Housie take?
faq.a: About 15 to 20 minutes for one full game with Jaldi Five, three lines and Full House.

faq.q: Is Shaadi Hai Housie good for a December or shaadi season kitty party?
faq.a: Yes. The "Shaadi hai!" call fits the wedding season, it needs no decoration or cooking, and everyone stays seated, so it suits ladies of every age.
